name: apt-get
description: The lower-level, script-stable APT front end. Same engine as apt with a guaranteed-stable output and option set.

flags.description: Install / remove (keep config) / remove with config.
Upgrade handling complex dependency changes (apt's full-upgrade).
Skip recommended packages — smaller, minimal installs.
Remove orphaned dependencies / delete cached .deb files.

examples.explanation: Refreshes the package index. Required before install on a fresh system.
The standard Dockerfile pattern: minimal non-interactive install of just what is needed.
Full upgrade that may install or remove packages to satisfy new dependencies.
Removes cached .deb files that can no longer be downloaded — reclaims /var/cache/apt space.

about: apt-get predates apt and guarantees backward compatibility, which is why scripts, Dockerfiles, and CI pipelines use it. For interactive use apt is prettier; for automation apt-get is the contract.
mistakes: Mixing apt and apt-get in scripts — pick one (apt-get) for automation.
warnings: Same engine and lock as apt: never run two package operations simultaneously.
